As per the statement of learned A.G.A., the informant has refused to take the notice.
2.

In the instant case, notice to the informant was sent by the Court also and as per the office report,
the same could not be served, as such, again the reminder was sent.
As per the office report dated 12.7.2024, the response to the said reminder is awaited.
3. Taking into consideration the statement of the learned A.G.A. that the informant has refused to receive the notice, the same is deemed to be served.

4. Heard Sri Mohit Singh, learned counsel for the applicant as well as Sri R.M. Yadav, learned A.G.A.
for the State and perused the material placed on record.

sentences.text:
5. Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No. 362 of 2022, U/S 363, 366, 376 IPC and 3/4 POCSO Act,
Police Station Majhola, District Moradabad, during the pendency of trial.

PROSECUTION STORY:
6. As per prosecution story, the applicant is stated to have enticed away the minor daughter of the informant on 13.5.2022 at about 9.00 am, when she had gone to school.

RIVAL CONTENTIONS:
(Arguments on behalf of applicant)
7. Learned counsel for the applicant has argued that the applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case with a view to cause unnecessary harassment and to victimize him.
It is stated that he has nothing to do with the said offence.
It is stated that FIR is delayed by four days and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.

8. Learned counsel has further stated that the victim is the consenting party, as is evident from the statement of the victim recorded u/s 161 and 164 Cr.P.C., whereby she has stated that she had called the applicant and had gone with him to Rudrapur and had married him.
It is further argued that the victim as per her own statement is stated to be 16 years and that a leverage of two years may be granted to the applicant on the upper side.
9. Learned counsel has further stated that as per her transfer certificate, the date of birth of the victim is stated to be 2.12.2006, as such, her age comes out to be 15 years and 6 months.

It is next stated that the said date of birth from the transfer certificate cannot be relied in light of Section 94 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 and also in light of the judgement passed in the case of P. Yuvaprakash vs. State Rep. by Inspector of Police, AIR 2023 SC 3525,
whereby the Supreme Court has observed that in the absence of records relating to the birth of the victim, no other documents except the Matriculation or equivalent certificate from the concerned examination board or certificate by a corporation, municipal authority or a Panchayat can be relied upon to ascertain the age of the victim.
10.

sentences.text: Learned counsel has further stated that the statement of the three witnesses of fact have been recorded during trial.
It is stated that although the victim has deposed against the applicant, but the factum of the statement of the victim recorded u/s 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. have not been denied by her.
However, she has stated that the said statement was given under duress and pressure of the applicant.
11. Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.

It is further stated that there is no criminal history of the applicant and he is languishing in jail since 25.5.2022, as such, he is incarcerated for a period of more than two years and his fundamental rights enshrined under Article Nigam Sharma vs State Of Up And 3 Others on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180639282/
2 21 of the Constitution of India stands violated.

sentences.text: In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
(Arguments on behalf of opposite party/State)

12. Learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the bail application on account of the age of the victim,
which is less than 16 years, and also on the ground that the victim has categorically deposed against the applicant in her statement recorded in Court.
However, learned A.G.A. has not disputed the fact that there is no criminal history of the applicant.

CONCLUSION:
13. The well-known principle of "Presumption of Innocence Unless Proven Guilty," gives rise to the concept of bail as a rule and imprisonment as an exception.

A person's right to life and liberty,
guaranteed by Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, cannot be taken away simply because he or she is accused of committing an offence until the guilt is established beyond a reasonable doubt.

Article 21 of the Indian Constitution states that no one's life or personal liberty may be taken away unless the procedure established by law is followed, and the procedure must be just and reasonable.
The said principle has been reiterated by the Supreme Court in Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another, 2022 (10) SCC 51.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another, 2022 (10) SCC 51
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned AGA has not shown any exceptional circumstances which would warrant denial of bail to the applicant.
14. It is settled principle of law that the object of bail is to secure the attendance of the accused at the trial.

No material particulars or circumstances suggestive of the applicant fleeing from justice or thwarting the course of justice or creating other troubles in the shape of repeating offences or intimidating witnesses and the like have been shown by learned AGA for the State.

15. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record regarding complicity of the accused, the period of incarceration of the applicant and the statement of the victim recorded u/s 161 and 164 Cr.P.C., although her statement has been recorded during trial, larger mandate of the Article 21 of the Constitution of India and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

16. Let the applicant- Nigam Sharma, who is involved in aforementioned case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant Nigam Sharma vs State Of Up And 3 Others on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180639282/
3 is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.

sentences.text: 17. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.

18. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
